webpage.text:
23 of the best hotels in Bali for 2026

The Island of the Gods gives generously when it comes to hotels, with accommodation options spanning the full spectrum from surfer-friendly hangouts to eco-retreats and opulent five-star hotels. Most of the action takes place along the south coast’s silver sands of Seminyak and Canggu, where you’ll find lively neighbourhoods packed with swish hotels, designer boutiques, beach clubs and no end of bars and restaurants. On the Bukit peninsula, there’s down-to-earth Jimbaran Bay and Uluwatu’s cliffside design hotels.

Unmissable Ubud is the island’s spiritual heart and the hotels here, whether budget or blow-the-budget, tend to tap into nature, wellness and the island’s rich cultural traditions. Bali’s soul-destroying traffic (and steep volcanic ridges) can make the west and north of the island feel inaccessible, but those willing to bear the long drives will be richly rewarded with untouched scenery and friendly locally run hotels.


Editor’s choice

 * Best for all-out luxury: Amankila
 * Best for couples: Mandapa, a Ritz-Carlton Reserve
 * Best for wellness: Como Shambhala
 * Best for the vibe: Desa Potato Head
 * Best for value: Stone House
 * Best for design: Capella Ubud
 * Best for families: Bulgari Resort Bali
 * Best for being immersed in nature: Buahan, a Banyan Tree Escape

This article contains affiliate links that will earn us revenue


1. Raffles Bali, Jimbaran

£££ | SPA | POOL | Best for a sense of serenity

Raffles Bali has just 32 ocean view villas set between an arc of golden sands and 57 acres of luxuriant frangipani-scented gardens populated with bright blue collared kingfishers, pink-necked green pigeons and plain tiger butterflies. A sense of calm prevails, with days spent taking gentle nature walks with the Raffles botanist, lolling between poolside cabanas and dips in the Indian Ocean, and trips to the spa for open-air Balinese massages and Melukat water purification rituals. Two excellent restaurants showcase the wonderful local produce, while the Writer’s Bar is the place to be at sunset — with a spicy Bali Sling in hand. Just a 25-minute drive from the airport, this hotel is an ideal first stop to ease in before venturing around the rest of the island. 

Read our full review of Raffles Bali


2. Four Seasons Resort Bali at Sayan, Ubud

£££ | SPA | POOL | Best for jungle luxury

There are few bucolic Bali views better than the ones afforded from the terraces at the Four Seasons Sayan. Expect to find it wrapped in undulating rainforest and mist-kissed rice fields, with the Ayung River flowing through its heart. Most of the villas are enveloped in tropical gardens designed to harmonise with the natural surroundings and have private pools and outdoor salas. There’s a gorgeous spa with hours-long wellness rituals and a rotation of visiting practitioners, and a striking bamboo yoga bale overlooking the river. Elsewhere, there are four bars and restaurants, with food ranging from Mediterranean dishes served poolside to a chef’s table of Indonesian classics.

Read our full review of Four Seasons Resort Bali at Sayan


3. Potato Head Suites and Studios, Seminyak

£ | SPA | POOL | Best for green credentials

Desa Potato Head is more than just another hip beachside hotel in Seminyak — it’s a creative enclave, with a beach club, a music studio, an amphitheatre, art galleries, a sculpture park, a ceramics studio, cold-pressed juice bars, slow-drip coffee shops and designer clothes stores. Its rooms are stylish and sustainable, with reclaimed wooden walls, baskets made by local craftspeople, biodegradable coconut slippers and zero-waste amenities kits which include reusable water bottles, bamboo straws and natural soaps made from wild honey and Indian figs.

Read our full review of Desa Potato Head


4. Buahan, A Banyan Tree Escape, Ubud

£££ | SPA | POOL | Best for getting back to nature

Bali has its fair share of exciting design-led hotels but this is one of the most original properties to have opened just about anywhere over the last few years. In the northern wilds of Ubud and built around a “no walls” concept, all of the 16 private villas, the restaurant, lounge and spa are all completely open to the elements. Wake up in the morning to a symphony of birdsong, mist rising over volcanic peaks and breakfasts of mangoes and papayas plucked straight from the tree. Spend your days cruising around local villages devoid of tourists in an orange VW convertible; receive blessings from healers and shaman at ancient temples; while away your nights watching fireflies flitting through the forest canopy from your hand-hammered copper bath.

Read our full review of Buahan, a Banyan Tree Escape


5. Bulgari Resort Bali, Uluwatu

£££ | SPA | POOL | Best for a quiet location

They say Italians do it better and, if a stay at the Rome-based jewellery brand Bulgari’s resort on the southern tip of Bali is anything to go by, it might just be true. Bali’s answer to Surfers Paradise in Australia, Uluwatu has more than its fair share of swanky hotels, but the allure of the east-meets-west Bulgari Resort is in a league of its own. From the ultra-private beach club only accessible by funicular from the clifftop resort to the team of butlers who magically anticipate your every move and a miniature Bulgari perfume placed on your pillow instead of a chocolate mint, this is a hotel that wholeheartedly embraces the notion of unfettered luxury.

Read our full review of Bulgari Resort Bali


6. Alila Villas Uluwatu

£££ | SPA | POOL | Best for ocean-facing design

With its latticed rectangular villas and much-photographed infinity pool, Alila Villas is the most architecturally striking of the hotels on the Uluwatu clifftops. Designed by the Singapore-based WOHA, it’s also one of the greenest: zero-waste, plastic-free and with an innovative water conservation system. The 65 villas are all about sharp angles, Jenga-esque slatted wood and natural stone, while the Sunset Cabana Bar, cantilevered over the cliffs, is aptly named. The local spa treatments, yoga pavilion and access to great surf below bring the influencers in droves.

Read our full review of Alila Villas Uluwatu


7. Capella Ubud, Ubud

£££ | SPA | POOL | Best for a romantic escape

This five-star version of a 19th-century explorer’s camp is pure fantasy; in the Keliki Valley, about half an hour from Ubud by car, two open-air restaurants, a spa, a swimming pool, 22 one-bed tents and a two-bedroom lodge have been seamlessly woven into the hillside, threaded between lush banyan, mango and jackfruit trees. Designed by Asia’s favourite luxury hotel designer, Bill Bensley, each is a masterclass in maximalism, with elaborate doors that took a year to carve and paint, clashing fabrics on the zip-up walls, woods inlaid with mother of pearl, framed rattan panels and brass monkeys climbing up the bed frames. Tally-ho!

Read our full review of Capella Ubud


8. Como Uma Ubud

££ | SPA | POOL | Best for chilling out

Como’s celebrity-frequented spa resort Como Shambhala might steal all the headlines but its smaller jasmine-wrapped sibling, with its breezy terraces, superb weekend brunches and thoughtful spa treatments is blissfully chill — and more accessible. Sunny white villas with ravine views are prettied up with pale checkerboard floors, intricately carved wood panelling and rattan chaise lounges. Walk along the ridges of rice fields, stretch with complimentary yoga and pranayama, book a cookery class or hop on the free shuttle bus into Ubud.

 * Read our full guide to Indonesia


9. The Legian, Seminyak

££ | SPA | POOL | Best for a quintessential Bali beach escape

The Legian might be as near as Bali has to a grande dame. When it opened in 1996, Seminyak was barely on the tourism radar, and its Indonesian interior designer Jaya Ibrahim wasn’t yet a big industry player. The clean-lined design still shines, from the classic triple infinity pool overlooking Seminyak’s surf-ready beach to the parquet floors and frangipani-scented tropical gardens. The 67 suites and 15 villas are all about a certain teak minimalism, familiar to anyone who has stayed at an Aman resort, and the spa, service and dining are similarly top-tier.

10. Amandari, Ubud

£££ | SPA | POOL | Best for getting away from it all

A favourite with the one per cent, Amandari resembles a traditional Balinese village on a ridge above the astonishingly pretty Ayung Valley. Each of the 30 villas is the size of a small village, behind stone walls guarded by fearsome statues, with rambling living rooms strewn with antiques, decks dotted with loungers and frangipani petals, and opal swimming pools. Drag yourself away and you’ll find an infinity pool, tennis courts and a temple-like spa.


11. Como Shambhala Estate, Ubud

£££ | SPA | POOL | Best for a total recharge

The Como Shambhala was a game-changing wellness retreat when it opened in 2005, and is still a leader in Ayurvedic holistic wellness. Everyone who stays in the 30 soft-lit, cocoon-like rooms gets a personal wellness assistant, whether they’re here for a detox cleanse, a lifestyle overhaul or just a few days of Pilates and good eating. “Living foods” are to the fore, all the water on the estate comes from a sacred spring, and the jungle-facing infinity pool is blessed daily by a priest.

Read our full review of Como Shambhala


12. The Pavilions Bali, Sanur

£ | SPA | POOL | Best for couples getaways

With its red-brick walls, stone sculptures and luxuriant greenery, the Pavilions may feel like it’s been a part of the landscape forever but you can actually pay with cryptocurrency at this boutique hotel. Its 25 villas make for smart homes away from home, whitewashed with rattan furniture, seashell chandeliers, stone decks and turquoise swimming pools. You’re in coconut groves but still close to the sweet seaside town of Sanur, with shops, restaurants and that fine white-sand beach just a short stroll away.


13. Hotel Tugu, Canggu

£ | SPA | POOL | Best for stylish stays

Lined with gargantuan beach clubs, Canggu has rapidly become Bali’s most fashionable beachside destination, for better or worse. The antithesis of the big brand hotels that have cropped up here over the last couple of years is the fantastical family-owned Hotel Tugu, which feels like a little world of its own. Pebble paths and wooden walkways lead between lotus flower ponds to grand pavilions adorned with intricately whittled teak pillars, beautiful antiques, unusual artefacts and jewel-toned fabrics. In the evening, there are beach barbecues, jugs of pinot grigio and lychee fruit punch, and Balinese dance performances to enjoy.

 * Best luxury villas in Bali
 * Best affordable hotels in Bali


14. The Slow, Canggu

£ | POOL | Best for hanging with the cool kids

There’s surely no more painfully cool spot in Bali than the Slow, a tropical-brutalist boutique hotel/gallery/restaurant with a vibe somewhere between 1970s Laurel Canyon and early Tulum. All concrete and bamboo, everything from the Reverberation Radio playlists to the Chris Searl photographs in the 12 minimalist suites have been obsessively curated by the owners: Ksubi jeans co-founder George Gorrow and his model wife, Cisco, who designs the locally made wabi-sabi ceramics. Canggu may have changed dramatically since the Slow opened in 2016, but a certain surf-boho ideal remains here, with plans to open a new clifftop branch in Uluwatu.


15. Fivelements, Ubud

£ | SPA | POOL | Best for a healing holiday

If mindfulness talk, chakra cleansing and fire rituals under starry skies are your (reusable) bag, Fivelements is for you. Most guests stay on programmes that range from three nights to two weeks, depending on how deep you want to dig, and include spa treatments and vegan cuisine that could change the habits of a lifetime. The villas are dreamy thatched-roof cottages with views of rippling rice fields or the Ayung River. If you feel the need to escape, Ubud is about half an hour’s drive away.

 * Discover our full guide to winter sun


16. Amankila, Karangasem

£££ | SPA | POOL | Best for a total escape

Bali’s three Aman resorts may be ancient in local hotel terms, but the Amankila — designed by late pioneer Ed Tuttle for its 1992 opening — is still one of the best. There’s a glorious three-tiered infinity pool that cascades towards the Indian Ocean and the location has always been special: tucked into Bali’s quieter east, amid the thick jungle of the sacred Mount Agung and overlooking a wild black beach. Most of the 33 thatch-minimalist suites have private pools, adding to the sense of escapism.

Read our full review of Amankila


17. Como Uma Canggu

££ | SPA | POOL | Best for living the Canggu dream

If a hotel epitomises the thrusting new Canggu, it’s the Como Una Canggu on Echo Beach — all curved concrete and whitewash, with a surf school and scene-y beach club. There are 32 beige-and-white rooms and 55 apartment-style residences, many overlooking over a 115m curving lagoon pool, including striking three-bedroom duplex penthouses with curving roof arches over infinity pools. With spa treatments borrowed from Ubud’s Como Shambhala, and brightly Instagrammable food at the beach club, this feels like the 21st-century digital nomad dream.


18. Stone House, Ubud

£ | POOL | Best for friendly stays

For those that say Ubud has become a jungle-hippy parody of itself, the little Stone House boutique hotel still feels like the real thing. You’ll be staying in the heart of the rainforest, with the American furniture-maker Walker Zabriskie and his ex-NYC partner Wendy Kassel. With six creative themed rooms — think canopied beds, Javanese puppets and rich local textiles — and fresh local dinners served at a communal table, this is one of Bali’s most warmly relaxing stays.


19. Hoshinoya Bali, Ubud

££ | SPA | POOL | Best for Zen in the jungle

Hoshinoya Bali brings a mix of Balinese jungle-thatch and geometric minimalism. A lagoon swimming pool courses through the resort, which all of the villas have direct access to, and there’s the constant tinkle of water from a traditional subak irrigation system. The spa has twice-daily yoga, while the restaurant’s set menus happily mix Japanese and Balinese. The best seats for evening cocktails are in the seven Café Gazebos — unmissable Zen-geometric cages that jut over the valley.

Read our full review of Hoshinoya Bali


20. Mandapa, a Ritz-Carlton Reserve, Ubud

£££ | SPA | POOL | Best for being treated like royalty

On an especially lush section of the Ayung River, the Mandapa feels like a romantic escape, but for the occasional whoops of passing whitewater rafters. Its 60 high-tech but regal suites are built around a Hindu shrine in the style of an ancient Balinese village, overlooking a series of rice paddies. With spa treatments that hold their own in wellness-obsessed Ubud, and a restaurant where guests dine in bamboo pods, this is Bali at its most rarefied — right down to the fact that everyone gets assigned their own patih, or assistant to the king.

Read our full review of Mandapa, a Ritz-Carlton Reserve hotel


21. Jumeirah Bali, Pecatu

£££ | SPA | POOL | Best for coastal appeal

This all-villa resort has a tucked-away location on the southwest coast of the Bukit peninsula with easy access to the airport via a highway (a post-long-haul flight blessing, given Bali’s horrendous traffic). This makes it slightly cut off from the local culture, but the resort does roll down to the broad blonde sands of Dreamland beach, where you can be mesmerised by surfers barrelling through A-frame breaks. The villas are spacious and sophisticated, with elegant cream and cornflower blue interiors, spa-like bathrooms with deep soaking tubs adorned with tealights and scented bath salts, plus dreamy terraces with large private pools. The spa and restaurants are suitably decadent too.


22. The Menjangan by LifestyleRetreats, Banyuwedang 

£ | SPA | POOL | Best for nature buffs

West Bali has mangroves, savannah, and an enormous national park brimming with rare wildlife, thrilling buffalo races, glassy coral reefs — along with very few tourists. There are only a handful of hotels in this area and none are as charming as the Menjangan, with rooms around the swimming pool and villas on the white-sand beach. Spend your days walking nature trails, horse riding, cycling, snorkelling and eating in the treehouse restaurant. The spa has three open-air treatment rooms and uses only natural ingredients plucked from the forest that day.


23. Gaia Oasis, Tejakula

£ | SPA | POOL | Best for an affordable escape

You’ll find this pad on Bali’s blackened north coast, after a two-hour drive along winding jungle roads from Ubud. And, though it takes effort to get to Gaia Oasis, every minute will feel worth it when you set eyes on this barely developed part of the island. The resort is split in two; one, Abasan Retreat, is in the mountains, with little wooden bungalows surrounded by tropical gardens humming with bulbuls and sunbirds; the other sits on the obsidian sands of Pantai beach lapped by the Bali Sea. There’s free yoga in the morning and you can make visits to holy springs and a traditional Balinese dance school. This is a great choice for those seeking a thoroughly relaxing spa break without wanting to splash much cash.

Additional reporting by Oliver Berry and Isabella Kliger

COMO Shambhala Estate (Ubud, Bali) 4 Verified Reviews

19.7 / 20(4 Reviews)

COMO Shambhala Estate makes a compelling case that — provided a spectacular setting in the Balinese rainforest just outside of Ubud, a spare-no-luxury approach to the accommodations, and a certain earnestness of purpose — healthful living and extravagant indulgence can happily share a home. Meditating in nature has never felt better. The massages with traditional oils are some of the most sublime in the world, and the resident nutritionist and Ayurvedic doctor can't spoil the pleasure of a delicious candle-lit meal in the canopy.

Each guest room, where Balinese teakwood and Chinese antiques combine with fairy-tale poster beds, is housed in one of five palatial residences. Whether by ingenuity or luck, fellow guests are rarely spotted. The residences are extremely private, not least because you dictate your own cocktail hour, massage schedule and mealtimes. In addition to the residences, there are one- and two-bedroom retreat villas by the renowned Japanese designer Koichiro Ikebuchi, each with its own heated pool and steam room. The two restaurants, Glow and Kudus House, are perfectly inviting, but after a day of yoga, guided hiking, biking or just spa-going, it's tempting to place your order from the room and let dinner come to you.

webpage.text:
The Wonderful Como Shambhala Resort in Bali

We’ve already featured a couple of amazing beachside resorts from Bali, showing you the beauty of this island and now it’s time to go in-land and show you even more of Bali. Thus, we bring you the Como Shambhala Resort, a gorgeous forest retreat for those who would like to spend an unforgettable vacation in the middle of the nature in this Indonesian island.

The resort features a whole array of amenities like lounges, dining rooms, private areas for lonesome individuals, terraced swimming pools and a private atmosphere throughout. Ubud is a beautiful area to watch from the guest rooms, with superb landscapes and incredibly tranquil natural sonority.

The rooms come decorated with draping white furnishing that resembles natural wood structures, traditional chattels and superb local finishing touches.  A night here costs $535, if guests pick standard rooms, while the private villa could cost you up to $3,570 per night. Although the last one is a bit pricy, you can enjoy cozy royal treatments, combining local tradition with worldly experiences.

[TrendLand]
